justifications.functional_suitability: R-01 is covered by Search & Catalog Service (Catalog Management Service, Elasticsearch Client Adapter) and Digital Content Sync Worker for digital items. Circulation & Core Engine and the portals cover the wider scope. Gaps: no explicit physical item inventory model, and the Search-to-Elasticsearch indexing path is unclear.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Elasticsearch in Search & Catalog Service, PgBouncer Connection Pooler, async workers via queues, and CDN/rate limiting support the sub-800ms target. Gaps: no search result caching, no autoscaling or replicas for search, and no latency budget or load testing; APM is only monitoring.
justifications.compatibility: Standards-based interfaces: OIDC/OAuth2 with the EU IdP, OAuth2/REST to OverDrive/Libby via Digital Content Sync Worker, SMTP/HTTPS notifications, OTLP and Syslog. Gaps: no library-standard protocols (MARC, Z39.50, SIP2, NCIP) and no anti-corruption layer for provider APIs.
justifications.usability: Each user group has a dedicated interface: Patron Portal (Catalog Discovery UI, Loan Management Dashboard), Staff Circulation App with offline caching, and Admin Console with reporting. Gaps: no accessibility or multilingual UI mechanisms (only localized notifications) and an unclear mobile channel.
justifications.reliability: Primary Database has Replication & Failover Component, EU Secondary Region Backup Target, multi-AZ Redis, async queues, Sync Circuit Breaker & Retry Manager, and offline caching in Staff Circulation App. Gaps: no stated availability targets, no redundancy for gateway, Search or Elasticsearch, and no RPO/RTO or queue durability.
justifications.security: Strong coverage: EU IdP with MFA/OIDC, JWT Validation Filter, DDoS CDN, rate limiting, mTLS and TLS 1.3, AES-256 and pgcrypto column-level PII encryption, encrypted offline cache, Patron Policy and override permissions, audit export to EU Compliance & Audit Logging Service, and EU-only residency.
justifications.maintainability: Clear decomposition into containers and components with single responsibilities: Search & Catalog Service, Circulation & Core Engine, separate workers, and a BFF layer. Async queues decouple workers. Gaps: the polyglot stack (Go/Node/Java), some inconsistent L3 diagrams (containers listed as components), and shared Primary Database coupling.
justifications.portability: Open technologies (PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Envoy, RabbitMQ) and AWS/Azure EU hosting enable cloud flexibility. Gaps: no containerization or orchestration or IaC is described, and the CDN and APM providers are named without abstraction layers; replaceability is implied rather than designed.

sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch sizing, sharding and replicas are unspecified
Rate limiting thresholds could throttle legitimate semester-start bursts
tradeoffs: Rate limiting protects search but may reject peak legitimate traffic
PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Elasticsearch-backed search with gateway and rate limiting is sound, but no caching, autoscaling, cluster sizing or load-test evidence supports P99 under 800 ms at 2,000 concurrent searches.

sensitivity_points: Index update path and refresh interval are undefined
No defined sync between PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch
tradeoffs: Indexing frequency trades freshness against search latency
Write load on shared Elasticsearch competes with queries
PERF-02.justification: The catalog service indexes records, but there is no explicit mechanism guaranteeing 5-minute searchability, no separation of read/write load, and no queue or CDC from the database; the freshness measure is unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch cluster topology and replica shards are unspecified
Search is a single container with no stated redundancy
tradeoffs: Replica shards improve availability but increase cost and indexing load
AVAIL-01.justification: Database replication and failover exist, protecting loan transactions via ACID. Nothing states Elasticsearch clustering, replicas or failover, so search continuity during a node failure is not shown; circulation is independent of search, which helps.

sensitivity_points: No multiple instances or load balancing of portal/gateway are modeled
Health checks and failover timing are unspecified
tradeoffs: Stateless instances ease failover but require externalised session state
AVAIL-02.justification: Portal is a client-side container and the CDN gives some routing resilience, but no redundant instances, orchestration or health-check mechanism is shown. Loan data is protected by the database's replication, so loss is unlikely, yet the 1-minute interruption bound is unsupported.

sensitivity_points: Provider client may lack an abstract interface for multiple providers
Metadata mapping to the catalog schema may leak into the persistence adapter
tradeoffs: A uniform provider abstraction eases extension but limits provider-specific features
MOD-01.justification: Isolated Provider Integration Client and asynchronous worker confine provider-specific logic to one component, with persistence and resilience separate. However, there is no explicit pluggable provider interface, and catalog indexing into Elasticsearch is unclear.

sensitivity_points: Loan rules location (code versus data) is unspecified
Rules per library tenant are not modeled
tradeoffs: Configurable rules add flexibility but complicate validation and testing
MOD-02.justification: A separate Patron Policy Component and Admin configuration client suggest a place for rules, but no rule engine, tenant-specific configuration store or runtime reload is described. Rules are probably in Go code, requiring redeployment.

sensitivity_points: External Notification Service location is not stated as EU
Third-party providers and OverDrive/Libby receive data without EU guarantee
tradeoffs: EU-only providers limit vendor choice and may raise cost
SEC-01.justification: Hosting, database, backups, CDN PoPs, IdP, logging and APM are all EU-bound. Gaps: External Notification Service and content providers are not stated EU, and no technical enforcement (policy, egress control) is shown. Also offline caching of PII on client devices.

sensitivity_points: Object-level authorization for loan history is not explicit
Denied-access events are not explicitly audited
tradeoffs: Fine-grained per-record checks add latency and complexity to every request
SEC-02.justification: JWT validation, an auth facade, a policy component and audit export to a compliance service provide the pieces. However, no explicit ownership check for loan history, nor logging of denied attempts, is described; the loan history is not named as an audited resource.
